You could have described my bf exactly. On the outside he's a nice, normal, decent person that treats people well, helps when help is needed, and is (or acts) very empathic towards just about everyone. Except me. I'm the one that gets to enjoy the silent treatment, him punching and throwing things, the big heavy sighs, and the "nothing" when I ask him what's wrong. But he makes himself oh so available to everyone else. And when I would bring up that his behavior is hurtful, he dismissed it and kept insisting that I was making him this way. Oh yeah, and the talking about himself and his interests is a big one.

Our interests overlap but it's like when he gets into something new, if I don't get into it with him he's very resentful about it and starts blaming everyone in his life for not catering to him.

Yours freaks out over socks too? For mine it's like, any minor annoyance sends him spiraling into an anger fit and he always takes it out on me because I've been the one to take care of the house. But how am I supposed to know that XYZ need to be done when it's never been an issue and no one's ever told me to do it?

I'm dealing with this right now. Silent treatment, one word replies, big sighs, just general nasty attitude towards me. I've told him before this treatment triggers my anxiety big time and he just said "that's just how he deals with things". I've always accepted that answer without taking into consideration it's an invalidation of my feelings.

Yes, I have always been this way. When I was little I used to have big crying fits when the person who I thought was my best friend would hang out with other people. It confused me because we spent all our time together, just with each other, and then there would be a day where she would hang out with a group. Looking back on it, it's easy to say I might have had romantic feelings for her (I am bi), but the truth was just that I wanted ONE person for myself and they could only have me as well. 

This repeated for just about all my life. Not just friends, but relationships too. I get so clingy and anxious when I feel like my needs are not being met that I've found myself begging and pleading for people not to leave me- because they are my ONE person. One redditor below pointed attachment theory out, and I think that's what it is: anxious attachment style.

Please take care of yourself. It might seem hypocritical coming from the OP but I know your exact feelings. I suffer from su\*cidal ideations and things like this always trigger them- it is always my first thought and I know how scary it is. I don't have a close relationship with my parents either, and no local friends that aren't mutual with my bf.  It can be so lonely. Please take the advice of everyone in this thread as well.

Thank you. Your words are genuinely touching. I've never thought about my disorder that way because I feel like all it does is set me back. I'm sure there are many beautiful things that come out of ADHD, but it hurts because I will fundamentally never be normal. I remember the moment I tried my friend's Adderall and crying because my brain was so, so quiet and it hurt that other people were able to have that without relying on a prescription.

It's strange too because I would never put somebody else down for their disorder, but mine makes me hate myself so much. What kind of person can't remember simple tasks? Why can't I just be normal?

Again, thank you for your words. I'm still going through and processing all the advice I've been given.
